title: List loaded kernel modules
summary: Show which kernel drivers and modules are currently loaded, for example to check whether a Wi-Fi driver is active. This only reads information and changes nothing.

aliases.text: check if wifi driver is loaded
проверить загружен ли драйвер wifi linux

prerequisites: lsmod is provided by the kmod package, which normal desktops install

steps.explain: List every kernel module (driver) that is loaded right now. The 'Used by' column lists the modules that depend on each one; an empty column or 0 means nothing uses it. This is read-only.
steps.expect: A header line 'Module  Size  Used by' followed by one module per line, for example 'rosetta  12288  -2'. Desktops show dozens to hundreds of lines.

alternatives.explain: Read the same list directly from the kernel's /proc file. Use this if lsmod says 'command not found'. There is no header line; the columns are name, size, use count, dependents, state and address.

steps.explain: Show only the modules whose name contains a given text, for example to check whether a Wi-Fi driver is loaded. No output means no matching module is loaded.

placeholders.name: MODULE_NAME
placeholders.description: Part of the driver or module name to look for

steps.expect: One line per match that starts with the module name, for example 'iwlwifi  524288  0'. No output means that module is not loaded.

verify.expect: The header 'Module  Size  Used by' and four module lines below it.

source.title: lsmod manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
